Title: Producing realistic climate data with generative adversarial networks
Authors: Camille Besombes, Olivier Pannekoucke, Corentin Lapeyre, Benjamin Sanderson, Olivier Thual
Venue: Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics, vol. 28, pp. 347-370
Why relevant / why suggested: Uses a WGAN trained on a GCM (PLASIM) climate to generate realistic multivariate weather situations, a foundational stochastic weather-generator GAN application distinct from downscaling/nowcasting.
First-pass evaluation signal (from abstr: Investigates whether the GAN can reproduce the climate's realistic weather situations; abstract does not clearly reference memorization checks or C2ST-style discriminators - not determinable from abstract.

Title: CliGAN: A Structurally Sensitive Convolutional Neural Network Model for Statistical Downscaling of Precipitation from Multi-Model Ensembles
Why relevant / why suggested: A 2020 Wasserstein-GAN downscaling method for annual maximum precipitation from CMIP6 multi-model ensembles to regional grids, an early foundational GAN application to climate extremes.
First-pass evaluation signal (from abstr: Uses Wasserstein critic loss plus MS-SSIM structural loss; abstract does not clearly discuss ensemble diversity, memorization, or discriminative (C2ST) testing - not determinable from abstract.
